lead: what you go looking for is always somebody you already had, and the pleasure is in the tracking — so the reunion, when it finally comes off, is the flattest part of the whole thing.
sun: an old number gets found, the cousin gets rung, the man who moved abroad in his twenties is at a table with you inside a month — and the group credits you with loyalty, which is a word for staying. what did the work was a scent, and following a person and keeping hold of one look identical from any distance.
moon: the appetite only ever fully engages on a person currently out of reach — reachability is what kills it — so the friend restored is the friend no longer interesting, and nothing underneath can tell those two conditions apart. the same face, at the same table, before the finding and after it.
pull: you can find anybody. the wanting runs on the distance, so the moment somebody is back in the room they stop being the person you spent four months looking for.
tension: the one who keeps everybody together is the phrase, and a decade of reunions backs it — three of them would not have happened without you, and everyone in the photographs knows it. none of them has been told that you were done by the second hour of most of them, and it cannot be said now, because every hour of the fondness was real while the looking was still going on.
cost: a first name, an old employer and one shared acquaintance is enough for you to produce somebody who has been gone fifteen years, and being found by you feels like being wanted. the ones who never went anywhere get none of it — nothing about them needs tracking, so the friend two streets away who has answered every message since school hears from you least.

lead: twelve times you have brought a wrecked thing back, so when the room saw you at full volume you set about that one the same way — and it is the only one that never came back.
sun: the retrieval went out the next week and it was competent: the calls made in the right order, the apology given in full and without conditions, the decent interval observed. every step of it you had performed before, on other people's behalf, successfully. the relationships came back, one by one, exactly as you expected them to. what has not come back is the reading, and forty people took it first-hand in ninety seconds.
moon: inside, none of it corrected anything. the register did not come down a notch; there is no lower one to come down to, and the belief that a mark can be worked off afterwards removes the argument for trying. what changed after that afternoon is where you let it show, which is a decision about rooms rather than about volume, and it holds only while you are watching.
pull: everything you have ever lost has been brought back to you. the one item still out there is ninety seconds of yourself, and it is being kept by people who like you.
tension: the apology was accepted by everyone in that room, and none of it touched what they saw. you read that as work still outstanding rather than as a thing settled, so you go back for it — a joke about it, a heavier version at the next dinner, one more conversation with the two who were closest. the incident is four years old and still gets an airing twice a year, and you are the one raising it.
cost: families that would have gone quiet for twenty years got the row instead, out loud, in front of everybody, and then got you at the door the month after — twice that has held together something that was going under. nobody in your life has been offered a small version of you, and the ones who wanted one left early, while there was still nothing to work back.

lead: you have never had a last anything. other people can name the final visit, the last night in the old flat, the evening the four of you were all in one kitchen. you have no such list.
sun: no room has ever been given your departure. you do not resign, you go quiet and reappear; there has never been a leaving party, a farewell dinner, a final shift anybody marked. so people around you never get the event — the moment where a thing is closed and everyone present agrees it happened — and what they have instead is a long unpunctuated availability that reads, from outside, as never having gone anywhere.
moon: an absence registers as out. the person is out of the room, the year is out of use, and no second reading ever arrives at three in the morning carrying the other verdict. so nothing has been mourned at the time, ever, and you have never found out what other people are doing when they do that, or where they keep it afterwards.
pull: you are the one who brings things back and the one who always comes back, doubled, with nothing in you that can perform an ending. nothing in your life has ever been over.
tension: people come back to you and find nothing to come back to. no gap where they were, no year of the door being watched, no evidence anywhere on you that the house was short a person — and the welcome is enormous and completely genuine, which makes it worse rather than better. the ones who went a long way away wanted to matter by their absence, and absence is the one instrument you have never been able to feel.
cost: nothing in your life has been lost past recovery, and somebody who wrecked a thing with you at twenty-four has it back at fifty on the original terms. every ending you have been in was performed by the other person, and you sat through each of them unconvinced. two of those people ended it a decade ago, and some part of you is still keeping the evening free.

lead: from across a room it reads as a sadness you carry. up close it is a household — the dead are still supplied here, at the old rate, and not one of them is counted gone.
sun: you keep the traffic going. his tea is still in the cupboard, the news goes to him first, the argument from that last year is still being had. none of it is observance — observance needs a death to observe, and nothing in you has issued one. so the newly bereaved find you within weeks: everywhere else their person went into the past tense by the second month, and here he is only late.
moon: what goes out has no meter on it and never has. an absent claimant is the cheapest one to keep — no arrangements, no visit to get through, nothing anybody has to be told — so the supply has never come up for review. from where everyone else is standing the whole thing flattens into a mood. nobody has been shown the hours, including the people they come out of.
pull: the dead are the easiest people in your life to keep feeding. they never tell you when it is enough, and from any distance at all it looks like nothing is going out.
tension: your sister has decided you took it well: no shrine, no bad anniversaries, nothing anybody has to accommodate. the person who lives with you has better evidence and no way to use it. saying that your father, eleven years dead, gets more of the week than she does would sound like the worst thing a person can say about a house in grief. so nobody says it, and the arrangement stays invisible from both ends.
cost: anybody in their first bad year can sit at your table and hear the name said in the ordinary way, present tense, by somebody not being brave about it — and there is almost nowhere else that happens. the living hold their own against people who never have a bad week, never contradict anyone, and are never inconvenient. nobody has told them a comparison is running.
